name: Question 9
problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(7,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}$ seconds.
worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $R=7$ and $\omega =2\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =7(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(7(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the velocity vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\,j \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\,j \\  & =-\frac{14\sqrt{3}}{2}\,i+\frac{14}{2}\,j \\  & =-7\sqrt{3}\,i+7\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

A particle P moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at O in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity of 2rad/s. Given that the particle is located at (7,0) when t=0, find the velocity of the particle at t=π6 seconds.

a
7i−73j
b
−73i+7j
c
7j
d
−73i
e
−143i+14j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius R in the xy-plane with a constant angular velocity ω is given by r(t)=R(cos⁡ωti+sin⁡ωtj), where it is assumed that the circle is centered at O, and the particle is at the position (R,0) when t=0.

In our case, we have R=7 and ω=2 rad/s, so we get that the position function is given by r(t)=7(cos⁡2ti+sin⁡2tj).

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

v(t)=(7(cos⁡2ti+sin⁡2tj))′=−14sin⁡2ti+14cos⁡2tj.

Finally, we find the velocity vector at t=π6, as follows: v(π6)=−14sin⁡(2⋅π6)i+14cos⁡(2⋅π6)j=−14sin⁡(π3)i+14cos⁡(π3)j=−1432i+142j=−73i+7j
